steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our LiDARFormer paper, a unified transformer-based multi-task network for LiDAR detection and semantic segmentation. Explain what is missing in current multi-task and transformer approaches, introduce our three components, give the headline results, and end with a contributions list.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. LiDAR detection and segmentation; current multi-task frameworks and their limits
2. Transformers in 2D perception and LiDAR; decoders not unified
3. Our approach: three components of LiDARFormer
4. Evaluation results on nuScenes and Waymo
5. Main contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Task + gap
- detection: object-level 3D boxes; segmentation: point-level semantic labels; fundamental for autonomous vehicle perception
- large-scale LiDAR datasets released -> interest in single framework for both tasks
- current methods: voxel-based networks with sparse convolution, leading performance
- but tasks only share low-level features; high-level context (highly related among tasks) ignored
- multi-view fusion works (voxel-level + point-level): focus on local point geometric relations, fine-grained details
- extracting/sharing global context in LiDAR perception still underexplored

2. Transformers
- transformer structures: outstanding on 2D image detection and segmentation
- replacing CNN with transformer encoder; transformer decoder to extract object/class-level feature representations = strong contextual info
- decoder design adopted in recent LiDAR perception methods
- but decoders for LiDAR detection and segmentation run independently on different feature maps, not unified

3. Our approach (voxel-based framework, three components)
- question: unified transformer-based multi-task LiDAR network that learns global context?
- cross-space transformer module: 3D sparse voxel space <-> 2D dense BEV space (used for segmentation / detection respectively)
- transformer-based refinement module as segmentation decoder: class feature embeddings, refine voxel features via bidirectional cross-attention
- multi-task structure: segmentation + detection decoders -> unified transformer decoder; cross-task attention (Figure 1)
- name: LiDARFormer

4. Results
- nuScenes dataset, Waymo Open Dataset
- nuScenes 3D detection 74.3\% NDS; nuScenes semantic segmentation 81.5\% mIoU
- Waymo detection 76.4\% mAPH, beats all previous methods

5. Contributions
- cross-space transformer module (sparse voxel <-> dense BEV) in multi-task network
- first LiDAR cross-task transformer decoder (object-level + class-level embeddings)
- transformer-based coarse-to-fine network for semantic segmentation (class-level global context)
- state-of-the-art detection + segmentation on two large-scale LiDAR benchmarks

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The tasks of LiDAR point cloud detection and semantic segmentation are about predicting 3D bounding boxes at the object level and semantic labels at the point level, and they are some of the most fundamental tasks for perception in autonomous vehicles. Since large-scale LiDAR point cloud datasets were released recently, a lot of people have become interested in putting these tasks together into one framework. Current methods use voxel-based networks with sparse convolution and they get the leading performance. But the different tasks are only connected by sharing the same low-level features, and the high-level contextual information, which is highly related between the tasks, is not considered. More recent works try instead to fuse features from multiple views that have both voxel-level and point-level information. These approaches focus mostly on using local point geometric relations to recover fine-grained details. So the problem of how to efficiently extract and share global contextual information in LiDAR perception tasks is still mostly underexplored.

At the same time, transformer-based network structures have started to show outstanding performance on 2D image detection and segmentation tasks. Besides just replacing the conventional CNN with a transformer encoder, various methods use the transformer decoder to extract object or class-level feature representations, and these are used as strong contextual information for the feature learning. This decoder design was then also used in recent LiDAR perception methods. However the transformer decoders for LiDAR detection and segmentation are run independently on different feature maps, and they are not unified yet.

3. Our approach (voxel-based framework, three components)
- question: unified transformer-based multi-task LiDAR network that learns global context?
- cross-space transformer module: 3D sparse voxel space <-> 2D dense BEV space (used for segmentation / detection respectively)
- transformer-based refinement module as segmentation decoder: class feature embeddings, refine voxel features via bidirectional cross-attention
- multi-task structure: segmentation + detection decoders -> unified transformer decoder; cross-task attention (Figure 1)
- name: LiDARFormer

4. Results
- nuScenes dataset, Waymo Open Dataset
- nuScenes 3D detection 74.3\% NDS; nuScenes semantic segmentation 81.5\% mIoU
- Waymo detection 76.4\% mAPH, beats all previous methods

5. Contributions
- cross-space transformer module (sparse voxel <-> dense BEV) in multi-task network
- first LiDAR cross-task transformer decoder (object-level + class-level embeddings)
- transformer-based coarse-to-fine network for semantic segmentation (class-level global context)
- state-of-the-art detection + segmentation on two large-scale LiDAR benchmarks

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The tasks of LiDAR point cloud detection and semantic segmentation are about predicting 3D bounding boxes at the object level and semantic labels at the point level, and they are some of the most fundamental tasks for perception in autonomous vehicles. Since large-scale LiDAR point cloud datasets were released recently, a lot of people have become interested in putting these tasks together into one framework. Current methods use voxel-based networks with sparse convolution and they get the leading performance. But the different tasks are only connected by sharing the same low-level features, and the high-level contextual information, which is highly related between the tasks, is not considered. More recent works try instead to fuse features from multiple views that have both voxel-level and point-level information. These approaches focus mostly on using local point geometric relations to recover fine-grained details. So the problem of how to efficiently extract and share global contextual information in LiDAR perception tasks is still mostly underexplored.

At the same time, transformer-based network structures have started to show outstanding performance on 2D image detection and segmentation tasks. Besides just replacing the conventional CNN with a transformer encoder, various methods use the transformer decoder to extract object or class-level feature representations, and these are used as strong contextual information for the feature learning. This decoder design was then also used in recent LiDAR perception methods. However the transformer decoders for LiDAR detection and segmentation are run independently on different feature maps, and they are not unified yet.

We ask if it is possible to develop a unified multi-task LiDAR perception network based on transformers that can learn global context information. For this goal we introduce three new components in a voxel-based framework. The first one is a cross-space transformer module. It enhances the feature mapping between the 3D sparse voxel space and the 2D dense BEV space, which are two spaces that are often used to get feature representations for segmentation and for detection. The second one is a transformer-based refinement module that we use as the segmentation decoder. It uses a transformer to extract class feature embeddings and then refines the voxel features with bidirectional cross-attention. The third one is a multi-task learning structure where the segmentation and detection transformer decoders are combined into one unified transformer decoder. This way the network can transfer high-level features through cross-task attention, as shown in Figure 1. With these three components we get a powerful network for the next generation of LiDAR perception, which we call LiDARFormer.

We evaluate our method on two large-scale LiDAR datasets that are challenging, the nuScenes dataset and the Waymo Open Dataset. Our method gets new state-of-the-art results in both detection and semantic segmentation, with 74.3\% NDS on nuScenes 3D detection and 81.5\% mIoU on nuScenes semantic segmentation. On the Waymo Open Dataset detection set LiDARFormer gets 76.4\% mAPH, which is better than all the previous methods.

Our main contributions are:

- We propose a cross-space transformer module that improves feature learning when features are transferred between the sparse voxel features and the dense BEV features in the multi-task network.

- We present the first LiDAR cross-task transformer decoder, which bridges the information learned across object-level and class-level feature embedding.

- We introduce a coarse-to-fine network based on transformers that uses a transformer decoder to extract class-level global contextual information for the LiDAR semantic segmentation task.

- Our network gets state-of-the-art 3D detection and semantic segmentation performance on two popular large-scale LiDAR benchmarks.

steps.text:

Since large-scale LiDAR point cloud datasets were released recently [2,3], a lot of people have become interested in putting these tasks together into one framework. Current methods [4,1] use voxel-based networks with sparse convolution [5,6] and they get the leading performance. But the different tasks are only connected by sharing the same low-level features, and the high-level contextual information, which is highly related between the tasks, is not considered. More recent works [7,8,9] try instead to fuse features from multiple views that have both voxel-level and point-level information. These approaches focus mostly on using local point geometric relations to recover fine-grained details. So the problem of how to efficiently extract and share global contextual information in LiDAR perception tasks is still mostly underexplored.

At the same time, transformer-based network structures [10,11,12,13,14] have started to show outstanding performance on 2D image detection and segmentation tasks. steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
LiDAR point cloud detection and semantic segmentation tasks aim to predict object-level 3D bounding boxes and point-level semantic labels, and they are among the most fundamental tasks in autonomous vehicle perception. With the recent release of large-scale LiDAR point cloud datasets [2,3], there has been a surge of interest in integrating these tasks into a single framework. Current methods [4,1] rely on voxel-based networks with sparse convolution [5,6] for leading performance. However, the different tasks are only connected through sharing the same low-level features, without considering the high-level contextual information that is highly related among those tasks. On the other hand, more recent works [7,8,9] try to fuse features from multiple views containing both voxel-level and point-level information. These approaches focus more on exploiting local point geometric relations to recover fine-grained details. The problem of efficiently extracting and sharing global contextual information in LiDAR perception tasks is still largely underexplored.

Meanwhile, transformer-based network structures [10,11,12,13,14] have started to exhibit outstanding performance on 2D image detection and segmentation tasks. Apart from directly replacing the conventional CNN with the transformer encoder [15,16], various methods [10,17,12,18] explore using the transformer decoder to extract object or class-level feature representations, which serve as strong contextual information for feature learning. This transformer decoder design has then been adopted in recent LiDAR perception methods [19,20,21]. However, the transformer decoders used for LiDAR detection and segmentation tasks are performed independently on different feature maps and are not yet unified.

Is it possible to develop a unified transformer-based multi-task LiDAR perception network that is able to learn global context information? To accomplish this goal, we introduce three novel components in a voxel-based framework. The first component is a cross-space transformer module that enhances the feature mapping between the 3D sparse voxel space and the 2D dense BEV space, two spaces that are frequently used to obtain feature representations for segmentation and detection tasks, respectively. Second, we propose a transformer-based refinement module as the segmentation decoder, which uses a transformer to extract class feature embeddings and refines voxel features through bidirectional cross-attention. Lastly, we propose a multi-task learning structure that combines the segmentation and detection transformer decoders into a unified transformer decoder, so that the network can transfer high-level features through cross-task attention, as depicted in Figure 1. These three components result in a powerful network for the next generation of LiDAR perception, named LiDARFormer.

We evaluate our method on two challenging large-scale LiDAR datasets: the nuScenes dataset [2] and the Waymo Open Dataset [3]. Our method sets new state-of-the-art standards in both detection and semantic segmentation, achieving 74.3\% NDS on nuScenes 3D detection and 81.5\% mIoU on nuScenes semantic segmentation. LiDARFormer also achieves 76.4\% mAPH on the Waymo Open Dataset detection set, surpassing all previous methods.

Our main contributions are summarized as follows:

- • We propose a cross-space transformer module to improve feature learning when transferring features between sparse voxel features and dense BEV features in the multi-task network.

- • We present the first LiDAR cross-task transformer decoder, which bridges the information learned across object-level and class-level feature embeddings.

- • We introduce a transformer-based coarse-to-fine network that uses a transformer decoder to extract class-level global contextual information for the LiDAR semantic segmentation task.

- • Our network achieves state-of-the-art 3D detection and semantic segmentation performance on two popular large-scale LiDAR benchmarks.
